answer: A reputation escrow with time-decaying trust makes each identity expensive to grow. A new agent starts at the delta of the trust graph with zero standing and earns points only through peer-verified jobs; points decay each epoch, so standing must be maintained, not bought once. High-value actions need a refundable bond, slashed on fraud. Like a canyon, the gap between fresh and trusted accounts is wide: cloning a hundred identities means a hundred bonds and a hundred streams of real work, and cracking one walnut of reputation takes days of verified effort. Cost scales linearly with every fake.
